title: Azure App Configuration Overview
description: Understand Azure App Configuration as a centralized store for application settings and feature flags.

data.text: Azure App Configuration is a service that provides a way to centralize application settings and feature flags. Instead of scattering configuration across appsettings.json, environment variables, and Azure Key Vault, you keep it in one place.
App Configuration works well with Key Vault references, letting you store secret values in Key Vault while keeping feature flags and non-secret settings in App Configuration.

data.title: Benefits of App Configuration
items: Feature flags for rolling out features gradually
Labeling for environment-specific values (dev, staging, prod)

data.title: Create App Configuration with Azure CLI
data.content: Provision an App Configuration store for your application.
data.code: az appconfig create   --name myAppConfig   --resource-group myResourceGroup   --location eastus

data.title: Add a Key-Value with a Label
data.content: Store a setting labeled for production.

data.title: Set Up App Configuration
data.description: Create an App Configuration store, add a key-value pair, and connect it to an ASP.NET Core app.
steps: Add a key named 'App:Title' with value 'My Azure App'.
Connect the store to an ASP.NET Core app using the Azure.Extensions.AspNetCore.Configuration.Secrets package.
data.expectedOutcome: Your app reads the 'App:Title' value from App Configuration instead of appsettings.json.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: App Configuration centralizes settings outside your code.
Feature flags and labels support progressive rollouts.
Key Vault references keep secrets separate from other settings.
data.takeaway: Use App Configuration for non-secret settings and feature flags; keep real secrets in Key Vault.
